reopen_history.reason: [replay:data_rebuild] The MIMIC-on-FHIR warehouse was rebuilt on 2026-08-24 after two upstream data defects were fixed: FHIR resources are now generated under UTC, so wall-clock timestamps are no longer shifted an hour across the spring-forward boundary, and Patient.birthDate is now derived from the anchor year and age rather than from the first transfer. This port was carried forward byte-identical to re-measure it against the corrected data -- do not re-author it. Expect previously accepted divergences to have shrunk or gone; if an hour-wide shift still appears, treat it as a finding and establish why the correction did not reach that path rather than accepting it as an upstream artifact.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Judge accepted the contested review: mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_outputevents.sql:9 casts outputevents charttime through TIMESTAMPTZ, line 60 writes the normalized value to Observation.effectiveDateTime, and lines 12,62-65 preserve the source value in Observation.valueQuantity.value; mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_encounter_icu.sql:31 casts icustays.intime through TIMESTAMPTZ and lines 97-99 write it to Encounter.period.start. Full-oracle replay exhaustively explains all 10 urineoutput conflicts with zero residual: five propagate through the judge-accepted divergent urine_output dependency and five arise from the shifted ICU first-day window anchor. The original 02:xx wall times are absent from FHIR and resource IDs are opaque. Candidate and oracle each have 73,181 rows, 73,171 are identical (99.9863%), and the 395/3,335,985 shifted selected outputevents rows (0.01184%) are consistent with DST-gap rarity. The current port preserves the dependency boundary, opaque key joins, LEFT JOIN, inclusive bounds, grouping, and SUM/NULL semantics; proven DST second-order damage is accepted under the contract as COMPLETED_WITH_DIVERGENCE.
